newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia interested in Saudi barley tender.
newsitem.headline: Australia interested in Saudi barley tender.

text.p: Australia was interested in participating in Saudi Arabia's tender for one million tonnes of feed barley for September and October delivery, Graham Lawrence, managing director of New South Wales Grains Board, told Reuters.
"Absolutely," he said when asked if Australia was interested.

Lawrence would not discuss NSW Grains Board's stock availability situation. Saudi importers would have to compete with Australia's domestic customers, its other export customers and the extent to which stocks were available or could be freed up, depending on price, he said.
Prices in the Saudi tender were hard to gauge because of internal trade-offs and hedges in trading companies, he said.

"My expectation would be that barley would be in the order of US$150 a tonne fob by the time it's loaded out of Australia. Depending on the way the weather goes, it could well be much higher," he said.
"Australian weather is a bit of a worry at the moment."
NSW Grains Board would not directly bid in the Saudi Arabian tender, with trade generally through trading houses putting up tenders, he said.
Significant quantities of European or northern hemisphere barley had not come onto the market. The Saudi tender would rely on old season stocks, which were tight, Lawrence said.
